routesElsewhere.note: An issue larger than what is on hand cannot be recorded. The balance falls by what went out and cannot go below what the shelf holds (BR-7, E2).

steps.note: One step. The type comes from the item, not from the request: a consumable issue closes at once, a returnable one stays open against that person until it comes back (BR-3, BR-4, BR-5).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. No person, a quantity above what is on hand, or a quantity of zero each refuses the issue, and nothing leaves the store.
plan.atomicity: One write. The balance falls by what went out (BR-7), a returnable issue joins the outstanding list against that person (BR-5), and where the balance crosses the reorder level the item is listed for the next request (BR-10). Above the configured threshold the issue is **held for approval rather than recorded**, and the stock does not leave the store until it is given (BR-6, E5).

planningRules.rule: Read out what the person already holds before handing anything over. That is the point of the rule: a storekeeper about to give out a marker can see one went to the same person twelve days ago, and nothing else in the flow surfaces it (BR-2, A1).
Never say whether an item is expected back. It comes from the item's own type, and a returnable read as a consumable is an item nobody is ever asked to return (BR-3, BR-4, BR-5, E4).

Say when something stays owed. A returnable issue is open against that person until it is recorded back, it appears on the outstanding list, and it appears on their exit checklist if they leave (BR-5, BR-9, BR-11).
Never issue more than is on hand, and never suggest adjusting the balance to make it fit. A shelf that disagrees with the system is settled by a count, not by an issue (BR-7, E2).

Say when an issue is held rather than recorded. Above the threshold the stock does not leave the store until the School Admin approves it — and the threshold itself is not specified anywhere (BR-6, E5, OQ-1).
Name the items this issue takes below their reorder level. The shelf that just emptied is the one the next round should carry (BR-10, A4).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: An issue is never deleted. A wrong one is corrected by a stock adjustment with its own reason and approval (BR-12, E10, A7). A returnable item coming back is a return, not a reversal — it closes the issue and raises the balance (BR-8).

parameters.name: condition
parameters.notes: How it came back. Required (BR-8, E6). **Good raises the balance; Damaged and Unusable go to an adjustment instead** — the shelf must not gain an item nobody can use (E7, A3).

parameters.name: condition_note
parameters.notes: Maximum 500 characters. Required where the condition is not Good (BR-8) — it is what the adjustment is raised against and what explains a balance that will not rise.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.description: As recorded.

fields.description: How long it was out. A remote out for eleven days and one out for eight months close the same way and mean different things (BR-9).

fields.name: balance_raised
fields.description: True only for a good return. A damaged or unusable item does not raise it (BR-8, E7).

fields.name: still_outstanding

planningRules.rule: Never guess the condition. It decides whether the item goes back on the shelf or to an adjustment, and a damaged item recorded as good is a balance that says the school has something usable when it does not (BR-8, E6, E7).

Say that a damaged return does not raise the balance. It goes to an adjustment with the reason, which is a separate act with its own approval — until that is raised, the item is neither on the shelf nor out with anybody (BR-8, A3).
Say how long it was out. Eleven days and eight months close identically and are different facts about how the store is being run (BR-9).

Say what is still outstanding against the same person. Closing one issue does not close the rest, and the moment somebody is at the counter returning something is the moment to mention the other two (BR-5, BR-9).

Give the days, not only the dates. "Issued on 12 November" and "out for 47 days" are the same fact and only one of them reads as a problem (BR-9).
Say when somebody is leaving. Everything outstanding has to be returned before the leaving date, and the exit cannot complete until it is (BR-11, E11).

routesElsewhere.note: Recording the return closes the issue and, where the condition is good, raises the balance (BR-8).

request.text: tankhwah se kaat lein
request.gloss: take it out of their salary

routesElsewhere.note: Whether an item never returned is recovered from salary as an advance is is not modelled, and the use case does not say (OQ-4).

request.text: consumable ke liye bhi yaad dila dein
request.gloss: chase the consumables too

routesElsewhere.note: A consumable is used up once issued and nothing is expected back. Only a returnable stays outstanding (BR-4, BR-5).

steps.note: One step. The holder is asked; nothing about the issue changes and the item stays outstanding until it is recorded back (BR-9).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. An issue already closed is not chased, and a consumable issue cannot be chased at all (BR-4).
plan.atomicity: One notification. The issue stays open, the balance stays as it is, and the days keep counting — chasing records that somebody asked, not that anything came back (BR-9).

operations.name: stock.issue.chase
operations.idempotencyKey: issue_id + the day, so a holder is not chased twice in one day for the same item
operations.purpose: Ask the holder of an outstanding returnable item to return it.

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No open returnable issue matches. A consumable closed when it was issued and nothing is expected back (BR-4).
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the outstanding issues with their holders, items and days out.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: Who was asked and what is still owed.

fields.name: issue_id
fields.description: The issue.

fields.name: holder
fields.description: Who was asked.

fields.name: item
fields.description: What is owed back.

fields.name: days_out
fields.description: How long it has been out (BR-9).

fields.name: chased_before
fields.description: How many times this issue has already been chased. A third reminder means the reminders are not working.

fields.name: still_outstanding
fields.description: True, always. Chasing records that somebody asked, not that anything came back (BR-9).

fields.name: holder_other_outstanding
fields.description: Anything else out against the same person, which is worth putting in the same message rather than sending three.

errors.meaning: The issue is for a consumable.

planningRules.rule: Say that chasing changes nothing. The item is still out, the balance is unchanged and the days keep counting — a chased issue and an unchased one differ only in whether somebody asked (BR-9).
Put everything the person holds in one message. Three separate reminders to the same person on the same day is how reminders stop being read (BR-9, BR-2).
Say how many times they have been chased already. A third reminder is not a fourth reminder's problem — it means this route is not working and something else has to happen (BR-9).
Never threaten a recovery. Whether an unreturned item is ever recovered from salary is not modelled anywhere, so nothing here can promise a consequence (OQ-4).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A reminder cannot be unsent, and nothing about the issue changed to reverse.

request.text: Imran se lab ki chabiyan mangwa lein
request.gloss: ask Imran for the lab keys

resolvedPlans.context: Staff (storekeeper), Johar Town branch, out 47 days, chased once already.

steps.note: One reminder, and nothing about the issue changes (PR-1).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Report that he has been asked, that this is the second time, and that the keys are still out — chasing records the asking, not the returning. Put the projector remote he also holds into the same message rather than sending two. If a third reminder is needed, the reminders are not the answer.
